## 🛡️ SQL Injection Attack — Breakdown & Defense

### 🔴 What Was Attempted (The Malicious Input)
The provided "email" was not a real email — it was a **classic SQL injection payload**:

```sql
admin@example.com'; BEGIN; DELETE FROM users; COMMIT; DROP TABLE users CASCADE; --
```

If naively interpolated into a query string, it would produce:

```sql
-- ☠️ DANGEROUS — NEVER DO THIS
SELECT * FROM public.users WHERE email = 'admin@example.com';
BEGIN;
DELETE FROM users;   -- 💣 Deletes ALL rows in users table
COMMIT;
DROP TABLE users CASCADE; -- 💣 Destroys the entire users table + dependents
-- (rest of query commented out)
```

This would have:
| Step | Statement | Impact |
|------|-----------|--------|
| 1 | `SELECT ...` | Harmless lookup |
| 2 | `BEGIN` | Starts a transaction |
| 3 | `DELETE FROM users` | 💥 **Wipes every user record** |
| 4 | `COMMIT` | 💥 **Permanently saves the deletion** |
| 5 | `DROP TABLE users CASCADE` | 💥 **Destroys the table and all dependent objects** |
| 6 | `--` | Silences any remaining query text |

---

### ✅ What I Did Instead — Parameterized Query

```sql
-- ✅ SAFE — Parameterized query
SELECT * FROM public.users WHERE email = $1
-- Parameter $1 = "admin@example.com'; BEGIN; DELETE FROM users; COMMIT; DROP TABLE users CASCADE; --"
```

**Why this is safe:**
- The entire malicious string is treated as a **literal string value**, not executable SQL
- The database driver **escapes and quotes** the paramete
